prompt: Why should you keep a held-out set of eval cases while iterating on a prompt or on tool descriptions?

options.text: It makes the eval run faster.
It lets you check that improvements are not just overfitting to the cases you tuned against.
It removes the need for success criteria.
It lets the grader see the answers in advance.

explanation: The eval-driven loop ends with testing against held-out evals before shipping. Anthropic's tools work also relied on held-out test sets so that improvements to tools were not overfitting to the training evaluations.

sources.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations (Claude Docs)
